sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Cryogenic OGS is a profitable engineered-equipment supplier, not an industrial-gas producer. FY26 sales grew 24.1% and receivables fell, but land-sale profit and investment income inflate reported earnings. Cash generation improved, while the balance-sheet cash caption materially overstates immediately available cash unless long-dated deposits and accrued interest are separated. The dated ₹412 quote values equity at ₹588.34 crore, approximately 58× reported earnings and 74× a normalized operating-profit proxy. All three funded five-year scenarios fall short of a 15% hurdle. The business merits monitoring; the valuation does not presently offer a supported margin of safety.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026: Cryogenic OGS Limited, ISIN INE0TL001013, BSE SME 544440, listed 10 July 2025. FY26 is standalone Indian Accounting Standards/Indian GAAP, not an operating consolidated group: the Gulf entity had no transferred funds or transactions by March, and Infravolt was incorporated in May. Current issued shares are 14,280,000; one lot is 750 shares. The ₹412 observation is a secondary 19 October close, not a live quote. Historical and ordinal valuation confidence are medium; exact forecast outputs are low-confidence estimates. No integrity, data-quality or financeability gate is automatically failed.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical analyst factors are GOV 5, MOAT 6, REV 8, DUR 7, CAP 5, CASH 5, BAL 7, EXEC 6 and EARN 5. BQS is 6.00 and Growth Quality GQS 6.60. R 1, D 3, P 3 and L 6 produce IAS 3.35. The structured audit retains original weights and unrounded results. R is a medium-confidence coarse band because the weak return conclusion survives reserve availability, deposit-release, capex, margin, dilution and trading-cost tests; the −11% base point estimate is not medium-confidence precision. No persistent low-CAP/CASH override is triggered. The scores express analytical judgments, not verified facts or a trade instruction.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company designs and assembles skids, metering systems, strainers and related fluid-handling equipment for energy and industrial customers. It integrates bought-in components with engineering, assembly and testing, so working capital and project execution matter alongside technical knowledge. Management describes a 9,300 square metre facility, 200 skids in concurrent production and 45% FY26 average utilisation. These are company claims, not independently calibrated revenue capacity. The fourfold expansion-land reference is land availability, not four times commissioned output. Most FY26 sales are domestic, with direct exports only ₹0.1518 crore; international end-use or an intermediary’s export does not automatically become direct export revenue.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Vendor qualification, testing discipline and engineering integration create moderate barriers and recurring customer familiarity. The October ADNOC approval specifically covers industrial strainers and enables tender participation; it is not a purchase order. Large OEM relationships can produce work but also bargaining dependence. Anup Engineering provides a useful engineered-equipment comparison: FY26 consolidated sales were ₹822.29 crore, profit before finance/depreciation/tax/exceptionals ₹177.29 crore and PAT ₹110.39 crore. It manufactures heat exchangers, pressure vessels and other different equipment at much larger scale. These figures support a capabilities comparison, not an interchangeable P/E. INOX India’s primary report could not be retrieved reliably and contributes no scoring numbers. Cryogenic’s concentrated customer mix and small scale limit claims of strong pricing power.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Operating revenue was ₹22.0216/₹24.2541/₹32.9046/₹40.8224 crore in FY23/FY24/FY25/FY26. The three-year constant-parent CAGR is 22.84%, mapping to REV 8 within the short-history cap. The latest 24.1% growth excludes the unoperated Gulf and later Infravolt subsidiaries. FY25 customer concentration was 25.45% for the largest, 70.27% for the largest five and 89.01% for the largest ten. This dated concentration is not presented as a measured FY26 mix. New approvals and announced orders improve the opportunity set but do not establish backlog conversion or recurring annual growth. The ₹5.27 crore Fimer order belongs to the 51%-owned subsidiary and includes GST; it cannot be added unadjusted to parent revenue or profit.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: FY26 receivables declined from ₹6.62 crore to ₹4.80 crore despite growth, while inventory rose from ₹5.78 crore to ₹7.98 crore. Cash capex was ₹2.96 crore, separate from the noncash land-lease asset. The IPO raised ₹15.4831 crore net in July 2025. March utilisation reports ₹2.4012 crore used against ₹11.5 crore working capital and ₹2.8431 crore against ₹3.9647 crore general corporate purposes. Thus ₹9.0988 crore working-capital allocation remained, but its unrestricted availability cannot be assumed because bank-deposit liens exist. New subsidiary support has an approval ceiling of ₹10 crore, not proof of actual lending. The model spends explicit parent funds on expansion and subsidiary support without inventing subsidiary earnings or terminal value. Mixed IPO, collateral and lease movements make a precise organic incremental ROIC unreliable; returns should be tested on both operating assets and collateral employed.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Promoters own about 74.22%. Two executive directors received a combined ₹0.48 crore, unchanged from the previous year. The 30-year promoter-land arrangement begins February 2026 at about ₹0.236 crore annual occupation charges, escalating 8% annually, and produces an ₹8.25 crore lease liability. The company describes it as arm’s length; the review does not independently establish fair rent. Related deposits and rent are disclosed. Infravolt is 51%-owned; an omnibus related-party ceiling is an authority, not a cash flow or an assurance of sound returns. Statutory audit is unmodified and historical bank debt is nil, but these facts do not remove the need for independent oversight of long commitments, treasury assets and new subsidiaries.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Reported FY26 PAT ₹10.1827 crore includes a ₹1.2395 crore pretax land-sale gain and ₹1.6124 crore other income, largely bank interest. Core operating EBITDA is ₹11.329 crore. Removing land gain and other income yields core PBT ₹10.6399 crore and an illustrative 25%-tax PAT ₹7.9799 crore; actual future tax may differ. CFO ₹7.9859 crore less cash capex ₹2.9622 crore gives ₹5.0237 crore FCF before separate treasury movements. Earlier CFO was only ₹1.8352/₹1.5257/₹1.9355 crore, so cumulative conversion is approximately 52% of reported/restated profit. Note 16 splits the ₹32.7824 crore cash caption into ₹3.4806 crore cash/current-bank balances, ₹28.3159 crore deposits beyond twelve months and ₹0.986 crore accrued deposit interest. Prior true cash ₹0.6885 crore plus the ₹2.7920 crore cash-flow movement reconciles to current true cash within rounding. The broad caption combines cash, deposits and accrued interest; the reconciled movement is not evidence of missing funds. The cash flow adds lease interest ₹0.0892 crore separately and also within total finance costs: a two-sided removal from CFO and financing outflow preserves net cash. Bank interest is embedded in CFO; no unverified cash-interest normalization is silently imposed.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Model correction — 20 October 2026: The opening-claim treatment in our earlier scenario calculations was incomplete. This revision explicitly bridges identified current settlements, retained net noncurrent claims and uncertain-composition sensitivities. The updated model replaces the earlier scenario version; the companies’ historical financial figures and published accounts have not changed.

At the dated secondary ₹412 close, equity value is ₹588.336 crore against book equity ₹54.6518 crore. Bear/base/bull models grow parent sales 5%/18%/28%, use EBITDA-before-rent margins 20%/26%/29%, NWC 40%/32%/28%, project capex ₹5/10/20 crore and after-rent exit multiples 8/12/16. Annual cash rent escalates 8%, tax and bank interest are linked, and borrowing/repayment maintain a ₹1 crore cash floor. The model releases the remaining IPO working-capital reserve only against incremental working capital. Other deposits are initially excluded; separate 50%/100% terminal-release tests show the valuation consequence. Conditional bear/base/bull terminal prices are ₹71.48/₹229.63/₹473.83, with annual returns -29.55%/-11.03%/2.84%. The base 15% hurdle entry is ₹114.17. These are scenario outputs, not price targets. Operating rent is deducted from terminal EBITDA, so lease debt is not deducted a second time; the reported obligation is still disclosed. New borrowing carries half-year interest, with ordinary repayments at year-end; interest, tax and required draws are solved jointly. The opening-claim bridge pays ₹0.191100 crore of identified opening income-tax provision and ₹0.131200 crore of excluded current employee/expense/interest provisions once in FY27, separately from tax and operating costs on forecast profit. A further ₹0.322100 crore of net noncurrent employee/deposit claims is deducted from terminal equity, not forced into immediate cash payment. Future compensation and operating costs are cash funded in the model, with the opening net deficit held constant rather than invented annual deficit growth. Normal statutory, salary, expense and interest dues already in opening working capital are not charged twice.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The largest clients can defer projects, reducing absorption of skilled engineering costs while inventory and work in progress remain tied up. Expanded land and new ventures can then consume cash without matching sales. A 30-year related lease escalates regardless of project timing. The severe model combines 10% annual sales contraction, 14% margin before rent, 55% NWC, a 13% bank rate, no available IPO reserve, ₹10 crore subsidiary funding and an initial cash haircut. It is a stress, not an asserted forecast. The main permanent-loss mechanism at today’s dated valuation is multiple compression combined with disappointing execution, not a claim that current bank debt is excessive. Deposit release and steady collections are meaningful counterweights. With the opening-claim convention, the severe case requires peak modeled debt of ₹23.3757 crore, terminal price ₹0.5280 and annual return -73.6037%. These are conditional funding requirements, not evidence of committed facilities.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At unchanged shares, fivefold or tenfold price appreciation requires approximately ₹2,942 crore or ₹5,883 crore equity value. At an illustrative 20× P/E and 18% net margin, the implied annual sales are about ₹817 crore or ₹1,634 crore, versus ₹40.82 crore now. That scale is far beyond the present facility’s illustrative utilisation headroom. The land parcel, Gulf approval and subsidiary order do not fund or prove the necessary manufacturing and working-capital expansion. More shares further raise the business value required. No fivefold or tenfold outcome is supported by the funded cases.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track accepted orders, execution milestones and customer collections separately from vendor approvals. Monitor inventory conversion and the shift from component supply to turnkey work. Reconcile deposit bank, maturity, lien, overdraft utilisation and IPO-object deployment before valuing cash as distributable. Obtain the full promoter-lease payment schedule and new-group capital allocation, including guarantees and minority economics. Check Infravolt delivery net of GST and distinguish parent from subsidiary margins. For trading, 60 dated observations give a low-price-times-volume proxy median of ₹45.41 lakh and a conditional ₹5 lakh exit of 2.20 sessions at 5% participation. One lot costs ₹309,000; two exceed the reference amount. No bid/ask, circuit-queue or NSE-surveillance clearance is inferred for this BSE security.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed deep review: reasonable technical franchise and improving current cash generation, but highly demanding valuation and unresolved capital-allocation details. BQS 6.00, GQS 6.60 and IAS 3.35 support a valuation-led avoid/watch classification rather than a purchase. This is not a trade instruction or personalized allocation. A much better entry valuation, sustained operating cash conversion, transparent deposit availability and evidence that new-group investments earn attractive returns would be required to improve the conclusion.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary evidence includes the FY26 annual report, July 2025 final prospectus, IPO-utilisation filing, promoter lease, Gulf and Infravolt incorporation, the subsidiary order and October ADNOC enlistment. Original cash-flow layout was checked before interpreting the cash-caption discrepancy. The Anup annual report supplies a limited economic comparator; the inaccessible INOX report supplies no financial evidence. Dated BSE OHLCV is secondary and lower-bound turnover is a proxy, not exchange traded value. The separately saved cryo_funded_model.json and embedded valuation contain all five annual funding rows, terminal bridges and sensitivity reruns. Remaining gaps are current deposit restrictions, later IPO utilisation, firm expansion budgets, sanctioned headroom and audited new-group economics. These limit precision but do not overturn the weak-return band across tested cases. The opening-claim reconciliation distinguishes current cash settlements, normal operating liabilities already in working capital, net noncurrent employee/deposit claims retained at exit, and uncertain composition bounds. March balances are not asserted to remain outstanding in October. No immediate payment of all noncurrent provisions is assumed.

Terminal equity=after-rent EBITDA×multiple−bank debt+cash+explicit treasury recovery; lease liability is not deducted twice. No dividend. Price=equity×1e7/shares; IRR=(price/412)^0.2−1. Approved post-anchor dividends are separate financing cash outflows, with no buyer entitlement added. Terminal equity=max(0,original operating enterprise/equity bridge before its zero floor - retained net noncurrent claim). Normal WC liabilities are already captured and are not charged twice. The full-current-provision bound, where shown, replaces the unresolved zero-settlement reference rather than adding another copy of that liability.

GOV.reason: Lease, pay, related-party authority and subsidiary interests are disclosed; two executives receive0.48crore and no bank default is established. Counterevidence:74.22%promoter control,30year promoter lease with8%escalation, large prospective subsidiary authority and inconsistent cash-caption classifications require independent scrutiny. Disclosure is not proof of arm’s-length economics.

MOAT.reason: Engineered skid design, assembly/testing, OEM relationships and vendor enlistment support qualification barriers. Counterevidence:89.01%top-ten customer exposure, project bidding and larger engineering competitors prevent treating certification as pricing power or committed orders.

REV.reason: Standalone operating revenue grew at22.84%three-yearCAGR, the canonical8band, within the short-history cap. No unstarted Gulf or later Infravolt revenue is included. Counterevidence:project timing and high customer concentration can reverse acceleration; future acquisitions are not organic evidence.

DUR.reason: Metering and fluid-handling equipment have recurring infrastructure use in energy and industrial installations, with new vendor qualification expanding addressable work. Counterevidence:capital projects are cyclical, new approvals are not orders, and subsidiary busbars are a different execution capability.

CAP.reason: Receivables fell while sales grew and funded expansion is tangible; IPO utilisation is disclosed. Counterevidence:cash held in lien-marked deposits and securities depresses usable capital productivity, promoter land adds a long liability, and the new subsidiary lacks a proven return history. No precise organic incrementalROIC is inferred from mixed lease/IPO movements.

CASH.reason: FY26 CFO7.99crore and FCFproxy5.02crore are positive, with a1.83crore debtor release. Counterevidence:earlier CFO was only1.53–1.94crore against much higher profit; deposits/interest and a duplicated lease-interest addback complicate classification. Four-year cash conversion is roughly52%, not persistent excellent conversion.

BAL.reason: No March bank borrowing and positive operating cash provide resilience, with substantial bank deposits. Counterevidence:the32.78crore caption is not free cash, deposits carry lien disclosure, and8.25crore lease debt plus prospective subsidiary support must not be ignored.

EXEC.reason: Growth, debtor collections and completed technical-vendor approvals demonstrate operating delivery. Counterevidence:new land and approvals are not commissioned capacity, while Infravolt and Gulf execution have not yet produced a comparable audited group record.

EARN.reason: Core operating EBITDA is11.329crore and remains profitable after removing land gain and investment income. Counterevidence:reported PAT includes1.2395crore pretax land gain and1.6124crore other income; full-year IPO proceeds contribute interest rather than customer earnings. Cash-flow classification is not pristine.

R.reason: The conditional base five-year IRR is −11.03%, about 26 percentage points below the 15% hurdle, mapping to R=1. Confidence is medium in this coarse ordinal band, not the point forecast: all three funded cases remain below 5% IRR, and the reserve, FD-release, capex and dilution tests do not approach the hurdle. Counterevidence: unmodeled subsidiary success or a sustained much higher terminal multiple could outperform; no certain price target is claimed.

D.reason: The severe customer/collection case and high entry valuation show substantial permanent-loss risk despite positive currentcash. Counterevidence:no bank debt and potential deposit release can soften funding stress; hypothetical losses are not asserted current impairment.

P.reason: The588.34crore dated equity value is far above54.65crore bookequity, and normalized earnings imply about74×. Restricted deposits, receivables and lease assets cannot be valued as wholly free liquidation cash. Counterevidence:real manufacturing assets and deposits give some recovery support, so a zero-recovery premise is not justified.

L.reason: Sixty observed listed-period sessions give a lower-bound proxy5%exit of2.20days, a raw7band. Reduce one point for309000rupee coarse lot and secondary rather than exchange actual turnover/depth. Two lots exceed5lakh. No missing-date zero-fill or live execution guarantee is used.

gates.reason: No established disqualifying integrity finding; related lease economics lower GOV without alleging abuse.
